topic: All-AI-Jailbreaks: An Archive of Prompt-Injection & Jailbreak Experiments

Organized by research themes: instruction hierarchy, role/persona conditioning, response-format control, cross-model variants, adversarial robustness
Explicitly framed as a research/red-teaming corpus, not a guarantee of effectiveness
Includes a suggested evaluation workflow: isolated test env, record model/version/settings/date, compare across repeated trials
Contributing guidelines require provenance: target model, date, source, behavior being tested
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications ranks Prompt Injection as LLM01:2025 — the #1 vulnerability
Prompt injection occurs when user prompts alter the model's intended behavior or override instruction hierarchy
Distinguishes direct vs indirect prompt injection; both are top-tier LLM security risks
Provides the canonical industry taxonomy that security teams and researchers reference
NIST AI 100-2e2023 (updated 2025) defines adversarial machine learning terminology and mitigations
Categorizes evasion, poisoning, and prompt-injection-style attacks against AI systems
Concludes there is 'no silver bullet' against adversarial ML attacks — defense requires layered, continuous evaluation
Authoritative US-government reference for AI robustness and red-teaming practice
Open-source red-teaming framework for LLM security
Automates adversarial testing of prompts and agents against jailbreak and injection vectors
Represents the tooling side of the ecosystem: archives feed frameworks like this for automated evaluation
Defensive counterpart to jailbreak archives — filters/guards against prompt injection at inference time
Shows the defensive tooling landscape that jailbreak research informs

stats.fact: Prompt Injection is ranked LLM01:2025, the #1 vulnerability in the OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications.
The All-AI-Jailbreaks archive contains 19 prompt files spanning at least 9 model families (DeepSeek, Gemini, GLM, Grok, Kimi, Qwen, Sonnet, ChatGPT, Antigravity).
The archive is tagged across 9 security topics including adversarial-prompts, ai-robustness, jailbreak-research, llm-security, prompt-injection, and red-teaming.
NIST AI 100-2e2025 states there is 'no silver bullet' against adversarial machine learning attacks, including prompt injection and jailbreaks.
The archive was created 2026-08-18 and last pushed 2026-08-20, making it a current, actively-maintained 2026 resource.

angles: Review the archive as a structured research corpus rather than a 'how to jailbreak' list — emphasize the responsible red-teaming framing
Map the archive's 5 research themes (instruction hierarchy, persona conditioning, response-format control, cross-model variants, adversarial robustness) to the OWASP LLM01 taxonomy
Position the archive within the broader 2026 AI-security ecosystem: archives feed automated red-teaming frameworks and defensive proxies
Highlight the reproducibility gap: model behavior drifts, so prompts must be re-evaluated in isolated environments with full provenance
Compare the archive's breadth (9 model families) against single-model jailbreak collections to show cross-model robustness value
